edge_explainer: James Latham is a 269-year-old debt-free family timber and panel distributor that screened cheap on two numbers that do not survive its own annual report. The GBP 51.2M cash pile is not spare: Note 26 shows GBP 19.0M contractually committed and the CFO review shows a GBP 45M National Distribution Centre being funded entirely from cash with ~GBP 22.1M still to spend, which moves net cash from 21.5% of market value to 14.1% and EV/EBIT from 7.3x to 8.3x. Both of the screen's warning flags are also wrong, in the direction that would have made the name look worse than it is: 'melting' is an artifact of measuring against FY23, a year when a COVID-era timber shortage let distributors book inventory-holding gains worth roughly GBP 37M of extra gross profit across FY22-23 (gross margin ran 23.8% and 19.6% against a ~17% norm), and the negative free cash flow is simply the warehouse being built - strip the project out and maintenance free cash flow is 6.6-7.8% of market value. The working capital moved the opposite way to the usual trap: they restocked, they did not liquidate inventory to manufacture cash. There is also a GBP 14.4M pension surplus sitting in book equity that the screen could not see, which takes price-to-book from 0.88 to 0.93. What is left after all those corrections is a fairly priced, well-run, unbreakable little company - and one genuine piece of bad news the screen also missed: the reported FY26 profit increase is an accounting artifact. The pension service charge fell from GBP 2.8M to GBP 0.6M, and stripping it out shows operating profit fell 2% on 7% more revenue, because gross profit grew 4.4% over two years while overheads grew 17.6%. The market has been right about this share the whole way: it never capitalised the spike earnings and now pays about 11x normalised earnings. There is no own-history discount to harvest, no catalyst, no independent broker coverage, a 203bp round-trip cost, a close-only quote at our permissions, and a $22k-a-day size limit. Expected value comes out marginally below the current price. Good company, no trade.
